title: fix: install merges filled-in files, and guards read braces
headline: Install merges the kit's rule changes into files the owner filled in, line by line, and the guard that follows a command into another kit project reads braces, wildcards and quoting as the shell does, so it no longer stalls on an ordinary command.
alignment: v1.33.1 fixes the two faults the 1.33.0 workbench verify found: a filled-in core rules file kept its old rule line, and commands with a brace or a bracket timed the guard hook out.

items.text: Install merges a file the owner filled in and the kit changed, line by line against the release it last installed, after keeping a backup. A clash, text that is not UTF-8, a guard file or a link is left alone and named.
items.where: A filled-in file the kit changed
items.after: Merged; only a clash is left to you

items.text: The guard expands braces as bash does and reads a wildcard against the real folders, so a brace, a * or a [ no longer runs every project's guards and times the hook out. A command it cannot read is held with its reason.
items.where: A command with braces or a wildcard
items.before: Every project checked; the hook timed out

items.text: POSIX classes, zero-padded and stepped ranges, U escapes and a wildcard after a cd name the project they build, so its guards run.
A session opened through a junction or a short folder name finds its project's record.
Install's backups stay out of git in tracked mode too.
Status, the session notice and fold-back say install merges changed files itself, and name the ones left to merge by hand.

verification: Each fix has a test that fails on the code before it; the timeout was measured at 14 seconds on 90 records before and held at once after.
No rule text changed, so the recall gate does not apply.

decisions.decision: Hold what the reader cannot read
decisions.why: A command that builds more than 4096 names, or reads more folders than the cap, is held with its reason; checking every project instead timed the hook out.
A base is a release tag rendered to the hash install recorded, so an unreleased kit or a wrong tag never becomes the base.

decisions.decision: User layer rolled back during the build
decisions.why: The owner chose to put 1.32.0 back while 1.33.1 was built, so his sessions stopped timing out.

dimensions.name: Privacy
dimensions.result: Backups kept out of git in tracked mode

dimensions.name: Code security
dimensions.result: Three highs in the command reader, all fixed

dimensions.name: Gaps, scaling, test value
dimensions.result: Two highs in the merge and the test gaps, all fixed

fixed: A wide brace range or a lone * ran every project's guards. Fixed in c07f2bd and 6bea38e.
Bash spellings built names the reader missed. Fixed in c07f2bd.
The merge rewrote bytes that are not UTF-8 and kept no backup. Fixed in ccdbdee.
accepted: A retired file's filled lines stay in the old file; install names it (the owner, 2026-11-15).
A script that edits the stamp and plants a tag could pick a wrong base; a backup is kept (the owner, 2026-11-15).
The base is searched in the 40 newest tags (the owner, 2026-11-15).
A crafted command of 300 KB or more can still slow the hook (the owner, 2026-11-15).
